item.title: CALIPER: Calibrating HPC/AI Network Simulators
item.description: arXiv:2610.16477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Network simulation plays an important role in HPC/AI system research by enabling exploration of network architectures, communication strategies, and system configurations at scales that may be impractical to study experimentally. Existing approaches to network simulator calibration and validation lack a principled methodology that combines parameter alignment, constrained inference, and independent validation for collective-centric HPC/AI networks. We present CALIPER, a methodology for systematic calibration and validation of HPC/AI network simulators. CALIPER distinguishes directly observable system parameters from auxiliary parameters which are configured via calibration and constrains the latter to feasible domains consistent with the target system. We evaluate CALIPER's hierarchical, scale-aware calibration and its effects on parameter identifiability and generalization using collective communication benchmarks on a reference system with up to 64-nodes at the J\"ulich Supercomputing Centre. Validation results show that the calibrated parameter configurations identified by CALIPER predict system performance with less than 5% mean errors across scale-up and scale-out network domains. CALIPER demonstrates that hierarchical, constrained calibration can produce simulator configurations whose predictive accuracy persists beyond the observations used for fitting.
item.dc:creator: Seyyidahmed Lahmer, Daniel Seibel, Srijeet Basu, Arno Troch, Jayesh Badwaik, Subhomoy Bhattacharyya, Abubakr Nada, Debjyoti Bhattacharjee, Vinay Kumar Baapanapalli Yadaiah, Michael Peeters, Andreas Herten, Darayus Adil Patel

item.title: Distributed $(\Delta+1)$-Coloring in $O(\sqrt{\Delta}+\log^* n)$ Rounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.16575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a deterministic distributed algorithm for $(\Delta+1)$-coloring an $n$-node graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ in $O(\sqrt\Delta+\log^* n)$ rounds in both the LOCAL and CONGEST models. More generally, $(\deg+1)$-list coloring with lists from a color space of size $C\geq\Delta+1$ can be solved in $O(\sqrt\Delta\log(1+C/\Delta)+\log^* n)$ rounds; in CONGEST, we assume $C\leq n^{O(1)}$. The algorithm combines Barenboim's polynomial coloring procedure with arbdefective decompositions, degree reduction, and a short family of hash functions. Using the polynomial procedure in the degree-reduction framework already gives an $O(\sqrt\Delta\log\Delta+\log^* n)$-round algorithm when $C=O(\Delta)$. Hashing adapts the color space to the current degree and removes the logarithmic factor. We prove the existence of the hash family by the probabilistic method and compute it by deterministic exhaustive search, using unrestricted local computation. We also give an explicit variant based on lossless expanders that avoids this search and achieves $O(\sqrt\Delta+\log^* n)$ rounds for $C=O(\Delta)$.
item.dc:creator: Marc Fuchs, Fabian Kuhn

item.title: The Voter Model with Opinion Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.16684v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the \emph{voter model with opinion graph}, a generalization of the standard (pull) voter model that adds a notion of bounded confidence. In this process, we consider a finite set $A$ of $n$ agents. Each agent $u \in A$ has an opinion $x_u \in O$, where we model opinions as vertices in an undirected opinion graph $G = (O,E)$ with $|O|=q$. In each step, an agent $u$ interacts with another agent $v \in A$. In contrast to classical voting, $u$ adopts the opinion $x_v$ if and only if $x_v$ and $x_u$ are neighbors in $G$. The process is stable once all remaining opinions are an independent set in $G$. We analyze two variants of the process: the ordinary EdgeVOG process, which samples a pair of interacting agents uniformly at random from all possible pairs, and the productive EdgeVOG process, which samples only pairs with neighboring opinions in $G$. We show the following: - For every opinion graph and every initial configuration, ordinary EdgeVOG stabilizes within $O(n^2\log n)$ steps in expectation and with high probability. The expectation bound is asymptotically tight. For the productive EdgeVOG process, the expected stabilization time is exactly the initial number of compatible agent pairs, while $O(n^2\log n)$ steps suffice with high probability. - An opinion $i$ with initial support $s_i$ survives with probability at least $p_i:=s_i/(s_i+\sum_{j\in N(i)}s_j)$. Further, let $\mu = \sum_{i \in O} p_i$, then we show the probability that less than $(1-\delta)\mu$ opinions survive is at most $\exp(-\delta^2\mu/(2(\Delta^2+1)))$ for every $0\leq\delta\leq1$. -If $G$ has maximum degree $\Delta$ and every opinion initially has support at most $\hat{s}$, then no opinion ever acquires more than $\tilde{O}(\min\{n,\Delta^6\hat{s}\})$ agents with high probability. This yields near-linear stabilization bounds for productive EdgeVOG for a large class of configurations.
item.dc:creator: Petra Berenbrink, Thorsten G\"otte, Martin Hoefer, Tim Koglin

item.title: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.16778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cloud graphical user interface (GUI) agents send instructions and screenshots to remote planners, exposing personally identifiable information (PII). Existing placeholder defenses mask detected spans and reuse exact strings. Fragmented or changed forms can expose PII or break entity continuity across turns. PrivacyGuard addresses this private reference problem with source-linked sanitization (SAN) and a structured reference lifecycle (REF). SAN reconstructs fragmented or overlapping evidence and rewrites the complete source extent. REF links changed appearances to session entities and supports locally resolvable references without returning raw values to the upload path. In five-turn sessions scored against common gold, PrivacyGuard reduces audited source-value leakage by 33.55\%--82.60\% relative to the closest prior full-pipeline system in all four reader--language combinations. REF raises strict cross-form continuity from 0.04 under exact-value reuse to 0.81. In reference-required Android tasks, verified completion rises from 8/30 and 7/30 to 17/30 and 20/30. On AndroidLab, PrivacyGuard achieves the highest or tied-highest task-success point estimate among protection pipelines for all four planners. On PrivScreen, it reduces fixed-reader field exposure by 62.72\%--62.84\% relative to the same baseline. PrivacyGuard lowers upload exposure while preserving a locally resolvable task path.
item.dc:creator: Zian Yuan, Wei Li

item.title: Efficient Resource-Shiftable RL Post-training with Generative Rewards
item.description: arXiv:2610.16866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training with generative reward models (GenRM) has become a central recipe for improving large language models (LLMs), and it is also increasingly resource-intensive: policy rollout, GenRM-based reward evaluation, and policy training all compete for GPU resources. However, existing colocated and disaggregated systems rely on static resource allocation for these roles. Such allocation cannot adapt as each role's workload changes during RL and therefore leaves a role's resources underutilized. We present PivotRL, an RL post-training system that dynamically shifts resources among different roles according to their runtime demands. PivotRL introduces a resource-shiftable runtime built on a Global Parameter Storage, together with a unified mechanism that efficiently shifts role-specific context. A shift-aware scheduler enables sequence migration upon a shift, while a planner considers the aggregate throughput benefit and the shift overhead to determine when and how to shift. We evaluate PivotRL on a 128-GPU cluster using four model groups spanning dense and mixture-of-experts models. PivotRL enables resource shifting within seconds and improves end-to-end throughput by 1.81-2.05 times over colocated deployment and 1.50-1.95 times over disaggregated deployment, while preserving RL convergence.
item.dc:creator: Yanfeng Zhao, Haoyang Li, Sheng Lin, Yuming Zhou, Jiawei Jiang, Bin Cui, Fangcheng Fu

item.title: FORGE: Procedural Weight Generation for Sparse MoE Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.16890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce FORGE (Fast On-chip Rotor Generation for Experts), a procedural weight generation system for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference. Rather than storing and loading every expert weight tensor from HBM, we show how a compact accelerator inside each Streaming Multiprocessor can regenerate them on-the-fly from $O(\log^2 d)$ rotor parameters per projection. Per replaced layer, gigabytes of stored expert weights are approximated with under a megabyte of seeds. This addresses the dual memory bottleneck of autoregressive Sparse MoE decode, where per-expert FFN operations are HBM-bandwidth-bound at small routed-token counts and the aggregate expert footprint forces multi-node Expert Parallelism (EP) with all-to-all traffic. We realize the approach as the Rotor Generation Unit (RGU), a fixed-function datapath that generates FFN weight tiles without competing with Tensor Core execution. With 30% of the MoE FFN layers replaced across five Sparse MoE models, we estimate 1.3-2.8x higher system throughput at matched GPU count and 1.10-1.15x lower per-user decode latency at short context. In exchange, downstream accuracy on three model families falls below that of the same model fine-tuned without rotor replacement, and the replacement ratio controls this tradeoff. FORGE also expands KV cache capacity by 1.2-2.6x. It is agnostic to the bit width at which weights are stored, so it can compose with quantization. The RGU is fully implemented/verified in SystemVerilog at ~0.9% SM area overhead (0.032 mm^2/SM, 7nm).
item.dc:creator: Chanyoung Moon, Travis Pence, Daisuke Yamada, Jiaqi Mo, Yanxin Zhang, Vikas Singh, Karthikeyan Sankaralingam

item.title: Mixture of GFlowNets
item.description: arXiv:2610.17007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) learn a policy that samples compositional objects in proportion to an unnormalized reward $R(x)$. This makes them useful wherever many diverse, high-reward candidates are needed and oracle queries are expensive. In practice, a single GFlowNet often fails to cover all modes of a complex distribution, and the obvious ways to scale compute saturate: larger batches and data-parallel gradient averaging draw every trajectory from one, possibly biased, policy, so extra rollouts rediscover known modes instead of finding new ones. We explore whether this mode-bias problem (mode collapse in the extreme) can be addressed with a population of asynchronously trained policies which divide the state space between them. Mixture of GFlowNets (MoG) replaces the single forward policy with a community of $K$ independent GFlowNets coupled through one jointly trained soft classifier, which assigns each member its own region of the state space through reward shaping. Mixing the members under their learned partition functions provably recovers the target $p(x)\propto R(x)$. MoG exchange (MoGX) also lets the classifier route sampled trajectories: a trajectory the classifier assigns to another member is sent to that member and trained on there, with no importance sampling. We evaluate both methods by keeping the environment-interaction budget fixed while scaling the community size, turning parallel compute into mode coverage without extra oracle calls. On HyperGrid, across six reward landscapes and communities of up to $K{=}64$, MoG and MoGX keep finding new modes as $K$ grows, while data-parallel training saturates. On a genomic ideotype-design task, MoGX covers $39%$ of the $1024$ optima at $K{=}64$, against $31\%$ for independent agents and $20\%$ for data-parallel training. MoG also has a lower per-iteration synchronization cost than data-parallel training.
item.dc:creator: Omar G. Younis, Joseph D. Viviano, Chirayu Anant Haryan, MD Vasimuddin, Sanchit Misra, Yoshua Bengio

item.title: MCCL: Measurement-based Collective Communication Library
item.description: arXiv:2610.17091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collective communication is a critical performance bottleneck in large-scale distributed training. Existing libraries and synthesis frameworks compute open-loop schedules once, assuming a static topology and peak link capacities. In production, however, persistent gray failures can silently degrade link throughput and latency for hours, causing pre-computed schedules to lose much of their efficiency during execution. In this paper, we present Measurement-based Collective Communication Library (MCCL), a collective communication library that closes the loop between runtime network measurement and dynamic schedule synthesis. MCCL passively measures GPU-to-GPU throughput, detects persistent degradation, re-synthesizes the affected communication-intensive schedules with warm-started synthesizers, and hot-swaps them without interrupting training. We validate the complete loop on a multi-node hardware prototype and use simulations to evaluate cluster-scale scenarios. In our experiments, MCCL incurs negligible overhead (<2%) while maintaining high measurement accuracy (<1.2% error) and low schedule hot-swap time (about 12 ms). Notably, under gray failures, MCCL reduces training time by up to 4.99x over static schedules on simulated training workloads for state-of-the-art LLMs such as Llama and DeepSeek.
item.dc:creator: Michele Ferrero, Gabriele Castellano, Paolo Medagliani, Sebastien Martin, Roberto Morabito, Massimo Gallo

item.title: Protocol Choices Matter More Than the Aggregation Algorithm: Federated Learning for In-Hospital Mortality Prediction in Care-Unit and Multi-Hospital Federations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated learning allows hospitals to train a shared mortality model without pooling their records, but published comparisons of aggregation strategies rarely control the evaluation protocol. This study compared seven strategies (FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedAdagrad, FedAdam, FedYogi and FedCluster) on two federations built with one pipeline: 12 care units of a hospital in MIMIC-IV and 49 hospitals in eICU-CRD. Each strategy was tuned and selected on validation data by the same rule, and every comparison was repeated across 10 seeds with Friedman and Holm-corrected tests. SCAFFOLD ranked first in both federations (AUC-ROC 0.886 and 0.819) and in 17 of 18 variants, but its margin over the runner-up never exceeded 0.008, and a control sharing its local optimizer attributed most of its margin over FedAvg to drift correction. On the multi-hospital federation, federated training matched centralized training. In the care-unit federation, three protocol choices changed discrimination by more than the choice of strategy did: discharge-coded predictors (+0.038 in AUC-ROC), client-level SMOTE (up to -0.074), and evaluating the last instead of the best validation round (up to -0.084). Platt scaling on validation data repaired the risks distorted by imbalance corrections without loss of discrimination. Studies should therefore fix the protocol before ranking algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Tertulino, Ricardo Almeida, La\'ercio Alencar

item.title: Towards Resilience: Slice-Driven Orchestration of Mobile IoMT in 6G-Edge-Continuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.17296v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Emerging healthcare services, such as real-time diagnostics, remote health monitoring and computer-assisted surgery, require stringent Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees while operating under limited and heterogeneous edge resources. Existing Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) orchestration methods primarily focus on communication metrics such as latency and bandwidth, while overlooking edge resource constraints and dynamic adaptation to workload and user mobility. This paper presents a novel resource-slicing-based adaptive orchestration framework that integrates 5G network slicing (NS), resource-aware orchestration, and mobility-aware task offloading into a single adaptive system. IoMT services are assigned to distinct 5G network slices while jointly considering CPU capacity, memory availability and amount of storage, enabling more efficient service placement and execution. In addition, the system supports user mobility and dynamic task offloading to maintain service continuity under changing network conditions. SimPy-based simulation demonstrates that the proposed method enhances service deployment efficiency, reduces request blocking, and improves user acceptance while maintaining reliable performance across diverse IoMT scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Zeeshan, Hafiz Faheem Shahid, Erkki Harjula

item.title: Computing All-Pairs Shortest Communication Time Paths for Periodically Varying Satellite Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.17372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the problem of designing an efficient algorithm for computing the all-pairs shortest-time paths in time-varying networks, specifically targeting the dynamic topological characteristics of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations. We model such temporal graphs as $G = (V, E_t)$, where $V=\{1, 2,\ldots , n\}$ is the set of $n$ vertices in the graph, and $E_t$ is the set of $M$ time-varying edges considered over a total time window of size $T = M\tau$, $\tau$ being the duration of each interval in that time window. For such a network, our algorithm finds the all-pair shortest paths in $O(M^2n^3)$-time. A key advantage of our approach is its computational structure, which mirrors two matrix multiplication steps, first in the forward direction and then in the backward direction. This structure of the algorithm makes it exceptionally suitable for parallelization on SIMD architectures like GPUs, thereby offering a significant speedup over traditional shortest-path algorithms and enabling efficient, network-wide message routing in rapidly changing LEO satellite constellations.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Sinha, Dibakar Saha, Sai Puppala, Bhabani P. Sinha

item.title: Agency as a New Organizing Abstraction for Computer Science
item.description: arXiv:2610.17410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Advances in large-scale machine learning have enabled agentic AI systems: persistent, autonomous computational entities that pursue goals, initiate actions, and interact with open environments. These systems are often framed as applications of foundation models. We argue that this framing is incomplete: agency is also a candidate new organizing abstraction for computer science. What is new is not the concept of an agent, nor runtime policy generation per se, but its general-purpose, open-ended form, in which systems can synthesize courses of action from goals, observations, and memory, over tools and environments for which no complete task-specific model was specified in advance. Thus agency becomes a systems-level abstraction as well as an AI modeling concept. Where the process abstraction organizes computation around executing programs, agency organizes it around pursuing goals under bounded resources: a process executes a program; an agent pursues a goal. From this perspective, the recurring failures of deployed agentic systems (runaway resource consumption, behavior redirected by adversarial content, opaque continuous operation) are symptoms of structural abstraction gaps, not isolated engineering defects. We examine these gaps across six dimensions (execution, interfaces, correctness, oversight, coordination, and persistence) and argue that closing them requires coordinated advances in systems,
item.dc:creator: Ian Foster

item.title: DisaggKD: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Teacher-Student Disaggregation and a Fused Loss
item.description: arXiv:2610.17644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit. DisaggKD separates them across nodes: teacher replicas stream hidden states to the student, a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards equals the full-vocabulary loss in exact arithmetic without forming the full-vocabulary logits, and a prefetch ring paces producer and trainer. Closed-form memory and traffic models locate the memory limits of each layout. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B pair, the disaggregated layout matches the LM loss of the colocated run with the same loss and is faster than that run; our fused loss also lets a colocated run train on as few nodes at faster speed, while the split is memory efficient when the student spans several nodes. On the larger pairs, colocated runs with a fused loss still run OOM where the split trains, because teacher weights and student states fill the budget.
item.dc:creator: Ruixuan Tu, Yuyang Dong

item.title: Space-Time Parallel Direct Numerical Simulation of Rayleigh-B\'enard Convection
item.description: arXiv:2610.17942v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rayleigh-B\'enard convection (RBC) is a model for turbulent flow and challenging to simulate by direct numerical simulation (DNS). Adequate resolution of all relevant length scales requires very fine grids in space and stability restrictions can dictate small step sizes. In this paper, we investigate the use of parallel spectral deferred correction (SDC) as a high-order time-stepping method to reduce wall-clock times of direct numerical simulation of RBC. Performance results on JUSUF (CPUs) and JUPITER (GPUs) with two different codes show parallel SDC can offer some concurrency along the temporal axis plus larger maximum stable time steps. Taken together, this allows for a reduction of wall-clock time required for simulations over one free-fall time by having to compute fewer steps and being able to mitigate the higher cost per time step through temporal parallelization.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Saupe, Thibaut Lunet, Mathis Bode, Robert Speck, Sebastian G\"otschel, Daniel Ruprecht

item.title: No Truly Sublogarithmic-Round Algorithm for Distributed MIS in the LOCAL Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.18215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that $o(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n})$-round randomized LOCAL algorithms find a maximal independent set (MIS) with subconstant probability on some input. This shows that the 40-year-old $O(\log n)$-round randomized CONGEST algorithm of Luby and Alon, Babai, and Itai is nearly optimal. Our lower bound improves upon the $\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})$-round lower bound of Khoury and Schild and nearly closes the 20+ year-old gap between the $O(\log n)$-round algorithm and the $\Omega(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}})$-round lower bound of Kuhn, Moscibroda, and Wattenhofer. To close this gap, one must show a lower bound for a graph that is not locally treelike. We do this by starting with a $D$-regular, $\Theta(\log_D n)$-girth graph, with $D = \Theta(\log n)$. Crucially, this is not our final graph. We obtain our hard instance by \emph{replacing} each vertex of this treelike graph with a clique on $n^c$ vertices for some constant $c \in (0,1)$. We then replace each edge with a bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph between the corresponding cliques, with each edge present independently with probability $1/2$. We analyze arbitrary LOCAL algorithms on our non-treelike hard instance with a novel round elimination approach. We describe algorithms that output a set of vertices in this graph using two metrics: their \emph{occupancy probability} and their \emph{conflict probability}. Our round elimination framework takes an $r$-round algorithm and produces an $(r-1)$-round algorithm where occupancy and conflict probabilities collectively slightly degrade, but individually can significantly improve or degrade. This round elimination result is obtained by exploiting the lack of large biclique complements in dense bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs, which in turn allows us to bound the entropy of the output distribution for any independent set algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Seri Khoury, Aaron Schild

item.title: Fast and Flexible Spiking Network Simulations on Massively Distributed On-Chip Memory Accelerators
item.description: arXiv:2610.18217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studying brain function and dysfunction in spiking networks with realistic synaptic densities pushes simulation technology beyond its current limits. It requires simulations substantially faster than biological real-time to cover long model times and enable efficient iterative exploration, particularly when connectivity is plastic. The modelling community aspires to a $100\times$ speedup. Yet on conventional many-core systems this remains elusive, bounded by inter-node communication and memory access. So far, significant speedup has only been shown on a custom-built FPGA system. We demonstrate the potential of commercial systems with large distributed on-chip memory to accelerate brain research. To exploit the local SRAM, we introduce a group-based mapping and communication strategy tackling spike-routing challenges on massively distributed systems. On Graphcore IPUs, the cortical microcircuit runs at a record $22.7\times$ faster than biological real-time with negligible build times and a reusable compiled graph. By design, the algorithm makes no model- or hardware-specific assumptions, providing a general strategy for advancing neuronal simulation technology.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Mia Sch\"ofmann, Jan Finkbeiner, Jan Vogelsang, Susanne Kunkel

item.title: HULK: An Efficient Algorithm for Enabling Fast Bulk Bitwise Operations on Homomorphically Encrypted Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.18391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A wide range of important cloud applications, e.g., database analytics, graph analytics, and genome analysis, spend a considerable amount of time performing bulk bitwise operations (e.g., AND, OR, XOR). These applications often operate on highly sensitive data, making data privacy a critical concern. Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables secure computation on encrypted data without requiring decryption, ensuring privacy in untrusted and shared environments. We analyze 13 end-to-end applications across three domains (healthcare, graph, and database analytics) and observe that bulk bitwise operations take 62-100% of the execution time of the healthcare and graph workloads. The key problem is that existing HE approaches perform them with high-latency homomorphic operations (e.g., multiplication or lookup tables) and significantly increase the data size. Our goal is to enable fast bulk bitwise operations on homomorphically encrypted data by designing an efficient HE algorithm that reduces the use of these costly operations. To this end, we propose HULK, which performs two key steps: (1) it constructs bulk bitwise operations using low-cost homomorphic additions, which compute the Hamming weight of the encrypted operand bits in every slot of a packed ciphertext without any homomorphic multiplication, and (2) it decodes the result of an AND, OR, or XOR from the Hamming weight with a single indicator polynomial, keeping the result in the standard encoding. Across 13 end-to-end applications in healthcare, graph, and database analytics, HULK improves performance over the arithmetic approach used by prior works by up to 7.26x (CPU) and 6.65x (GPU), and on average by 2.32x/1.78x/1.45x (CPU) and 2.08x/1.70x/1.51x (GPU) for healthcare/graph/database analytics. When we increase the reduction depth in a representative application, HULK's speedup grows to 10.10x over the state-of-the-art GPU baseline.
item.dc:creator: Mayank Kabra, Phillip Widdowson, Harshita Gupta, Rakesh Nadig, Nisa Bostanc{\i}, Eirini Tzermpou, Rakesh Kumar, Spiros Galanopoulos, Ataberk Olgun, Abdullah Giray Ya\u{g}l{\i}k\c{c}{\i}, Mohammad Sadrosadati, Onur Mutlu

item.title: An Asynchronous Maximum Independent Set Algorithm by Myopic Luminous Robots on Grids
item.description: arXiv:2012.03399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of constructing a maximum independent set with mobile myopic luminous robots on a grid network whose size is finite but unknown to the robots. In this setting, the robots enter the grid network one-by-one from a corner of the grid, and they eventually have to be disseminated on the grid nodes so that the occupied positions form a maximum independent set of the network. We assume that robots are asynchronous, anonymous, silent, and they execute the same distributed algorithm. In this paper, we propose two algorithms: The first one assumes the number of light colors of each robot is three and the visible range is two, but uses additional strong assumptions of port-numbering for each node. To delete this assumption, the second one assumes the number of light colors of each robot is seven and the visible range is three. In both algorithms, the number of movements is $O(n(L+l))$ steps where $n$ is the number of nodes and $L$ and $l$ are the grid dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Sayaka Kamei, S\'ebastien Tixeuil

item.title: Throughput-Oriented LLM Inference via KV-Activation Hybrid Caching with a Single GPU
item.description: arXiv:2501.01792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) with growing model sizes use many GPUs to meet memory capacity requirements, incurring substantial costs for token generation. To provide cost-effective LLM inference with relaxed latency constraints, recent studies proposed to expand GPU memory by leveraging the host memory. However, in such host memory offloading, the host-GPU interconnect becomes a performance bottleneck for the transfer of weights and key-value (KV) cache entries, causing the underutilization of GPUs. To address the challenge, we introduce CAPTURE, an LLM inference system with KV-activation hybrid caching. The activation cache stores activation checkpoints instead of keys and values during intermediate inference stages, requiring half of the memory capacity compared to the conventional KV cache. While model parameters are transferred to GPU from host memory, idle GPU resources can be utilized for the partial recomputation. To balance the latency of activation recomputation and parameter loading, our KV-activation hybrid caching scheme determines the optimal ratio between KV and activation caches to manage both recomputation time and data transfer times. CAPTURE achieves 2.19x throughput improvement over the state-of-the-art prior work for offloading both model weights and KV cache.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: The 43rd IEEE International Conference on Computer Design, 2025
item.dc:creator: Sanghyeon Lee, Hongbeen Kim, Soojin Hwang, Guseul Heo, Minwoo Noh, Jaehyuk Huh

item.title: Flex: Grid-Responsive Provisioning and Scheduling for Elastic Cloud Clusters
item.description: arXiv:2505.18357v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computing energy demand and grid capacity growth are at a crossroads. Data centers are becoming large, concentrated electricity consumers just as power grids face capacity shortages while also integrating more variable renewable generation, causing grid conditions to change significantly across hours and seasons. These variations create an opportunity for \emph{grid-responsive} operations, in which workloads are shifted to align energy use with time-varying grid conditions, prioritizing clean, low-cost periods of surplus generation and low congestion. Fortunately, a significant fraction of computing demand comes from batch jobs that are delay-tolerant and elastic, enabling clusters to shift or scale jobs, or adjust the provisioned capacity in response to grid conditions. However, provisioning and scheduling decisions are closely coupled. Effective cluster capacity depends on how jobs are scaled, while job-scaling decisions depend on the available capacity. At the same time, exogenous grid signals (\eg carbon intensity and electricity prices) determine the cost of both scheduling and provisioning decisions. To address this problem, we present \Flex, a grid-responsive resource manager for elastic cloud clusters that coordinates provisioning of cluster capacity and scheduling of elastic batch jobs. Flex takes a data-driven approach, periodically learning optimal scheduling and provisioning decisions based on recent history and reusing them to guide coherent runtime provisioning and scheduling. We implement Flex on top of AWS ParallelCluster and evaluate it using real-world workload traces and grid signals, including carbon intensity and electricity prices. Our results show that Flex reduces carbon emissions by up to $\sim$57\%, within 2.1\% of the oracle, and electricity costs by up to 60\% relative to signal-agnostic baselines.
item.dc:creator: Walid A. Hanafy, Li Wu, David Irwin, Prashant Shenoy

item.title: The ArborX library: version 2.0
item.description: arXiv:2507.23700v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides an overview of the 2.0 release of the ArborX library, a performance portable geometric search library based on Kokkos. We describe the major changes in ArborX 2.0 including a new interface for the library to support a wider range of user problems, new search data structures (brute force, distributed), support for user functions to be executed on the results (callbacks), and an expanded set of the supported algorithms (ray tracing, clustering).
item.dc:creator: Andrey Prokopenko, Daniel Arndt, Damien Lebrun-Grandi\'e, Bruno Turcksin

item.title: Metadata-Guided Adaptable Frequency Scaling across Heterogeneous Applications and Devices
item.description: arXiv:2509.22707v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling is essential for enhancing energy efficiency in mobile platforms. However, traditional heuristic-based governors are increasingly inadequate for managing the complexity of heterogeneous System-on-Chip designs and diverse application workloads. Although reinforcement learning approaches offer improved performance, their poor generalization capability and reliance on extensive retraining for each hardware and application combination leads to significant deployment costs. In this work, we observe that device and application metadata inherently encapsulate valuable knowledge for DVFS, presenting an opportunity to overcome these limitations. We formulate DVFS for heterogeneous devices and applications as a multi-task reinforcement learning problem. We introduce MetaDVFS, which is a metadata-guided framework that systematically leverages metadata to discover and transfer shared knowledge across DVFS tasks. MetaDVFS can output a set of DVFS models with significant generalization capability for various applications of heterogeneous devices. Evaluations on five Google Pixel devices running six applications show that MetaDVFS achieves up to 17% improvement in Performance-Power Ratio and up to 26% improvement in Quality of Experience. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, MetaDVFS delivers 70.8% faster adaptation and 5.8-27.6% higher performance over standalone device-application specific training, while avoiding negative transfer effects. These results establish MetaDVFS as an effective and scalable solution for DVFS deployment in heterogeneous mobile environments.
item.dc:creator: Jinqi Yan, Fang He, Qianlong Sang, Bifeng Tong, Peng Sun, Yili Gong, Chuang Hu, Dazhao Cheng

item.title: PerCache: Predictive Hierarchical Cache for RAG Applications on Mobile Devices
item.description: arXiv:2601.11553v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has become a de facto paradigm in various large language model (LLM)-driven applications on mobile devices, such as mobile assistants leveraging personal emails or meeting records. However, due to lengthy prompts and resource constraints, mobile RAG systems exhibit significantly high response latency. To address this issue, one promising approach is to reuse intermediate computational results across different queries to eliminate redundant computation. But most existing approaches, such as key-value (KV) cache reuse and semantic cache reuse, are designed for cloud settings and perform poorly on mobile devices as they overlook the distinctive characteristics of mobile RAG. We propose PerCache, a novel hierarchical cache framework designed for reducing end-to-end latency of personalized RAG applications on mobile platforms. PerCache adopts a hierarchical architecture that progressively matches similar queries and query-key-value (QKV) cache to maximize the reuse of intermediate results at different computing stages. To improve cache hit rate, PerCache applies a predictive method to populate the cache with queries that are likely to be raised in the future. In addition, PerCache can adapt its configurations to dynamic system loads, aiming to maximize caching utility with constrained resource consumption. We implement PerCache on top of an existing mobile LLM inference engine and deploy it on commodity mobile phones. Extensive evaluations show that PerCache achieves the lowest average end-to-end latency across five datasets and two LLM architectures, reducing latency by up to 63.5% over the strongest baseline while maintaining comparable answer quality.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwei Liu, Liekang Zeng, Lilin Xu, Bufang Yang, Zhenyu Yan

item.title: Circumventing the CAP Theorem with Open {\AE}thernet
item.description: arXiv:2602.21182v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The CAP theorem is routinely treated as a systems law: under network partition, a replicated service must sacrifice either consistency or availability. The theorem is correct within its standard asynchronous network model, but operational practice depends on where partition-like phenomena become observable and on how lower layers discard or preserve semantic information about message fate. This paper argues that Open {\AE}thernet (OAE) shifts the engineering regime in which CAP tradeoffs become application-visible by (i) replacing fire-and-forget link semantics with bounded-time bilateral reconciliation of endpoint state -- the property we call bisynchrony -- and (ii) avoiding Clos funnel points via an octavalent mesh in which each node can act as the root of a locally repaired spanning tree. The result is not the elimination of hard graph cuts, but a drastic reduction in the frequency and duration of application-visible "soft partitions" by detecting and healing dominant fabric faults within hundreds of nanoseconds, under the link-fault model and repair rule stated in the paper. We connect this view to Brewer's original CAP framing, the formalization by Gilbert and Lynch, the CAL theorem of Lee et al., which replaces binary partition tolerance with a quantitative measure of apparent latency, and Abadi's PACELC extension.
item.dc:creator: Paul Borrill

item.title: Leveraging SIMD for Accelerating Large-number Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2604.21566v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large-number arithmetic, widely used in scientific computing and cryptography, has seen limited adoption of single instruction, multiple data (SIMD) parallelism on modern CPUs due to the inherent dependencies in traditional algorithms. We present DigitsOnTurbo (DoT), which restructures the computation around independent, data-parallel operations, rather than vectorizing the standard algorithms, thereby leveraging the benefits provided by SIMD. Over prior SIMD implementations, DoT achieves up to 1.85x speedups for addition and subtraction, and 2.3x for multiplication. When integrated into state-of-the-art libraries (e.g., GMP, OpenSSL), DoT yields up to 4x speedup for addition and subtraction, and up to 2x speedup for multiplication, cascading into end-to-end throughput gains of up to 15.8% for scientific computations, and up to 5.6% latency and 6.2% throughput improvements on cryptographic implementations.
item.dc:creator: Subhrajit Das, Abhishek Bichhawat, Yuvraj Patel

item.title: Dynamic Resource Management in Production HPC Clusters
item.description: arXiv:2606.13266v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many large-scale scientific applications exhibit time-varying behavior, yet production HPC clusters still rely on rigid, fixed-size allocations, and most dynamic techniques remain confined to laboratory prototypes. This work presents a practical MPI malleability methodology that integrates with state-of-the-art high-performance computing (HPC) software stacks and operational practices. The methodology is implemented in the Dynamic Management of Resources (DMR) framework and is designed to ease adoption by existing applications without requiring intrusive code changes or scheduler modifications. We evaluate our approach by integrating the DMR API into two large-scale scientific applications and deploying them on three TOP500 supercomputers under realistic production configurations. Our non-invasive malleability solution achieves performance comparable to static baselines in controlled environments while substantially reducing node-hour consumption for identical workloads. These results show that malleability can be effectively exploited on production systems using vanilla resource managers, lowering the barrier to adoption of dynamic resource management in HPC.

item.title: Energy-Aware Scheduling for Serverless LLM Serving on Shared GPUs
item.description: arXiv:2606.30391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As LLM inference becomes a major cloud workload, its growing energy footprint makes cluster-wide energy optimization increasingly important. Serverless LLM serving helps platforms absorb traffic volatility by elastically sharing GPU resources across models, but this sharing also makes energy optimization difficult. Multiple co-resident models run under one device-wide operating point, while their resource demands and latency slack change across execution phases and load conditions. As a result, minimizing energy requires coordinated scheduling across request placement, runtime resource adaptation, and workload consolidation. We present Festina, a profiling-guided, power-aware control plane to minimize cluster-wide energy for serverless LLM serving. Unlike common global-local schedulers that focus on throughput or tail latency, Festina makes energy-first decisions by jointly coordinating request placement, SM partitioning, and GPU operating points under TTFT/TBT SLOs. In our system, a lightweight global scheduler performs fast, SLO-safe, energy-aware placement using constant-time lookups from offline profiles and GPU state summaries. On each GPU, a phase-aware local scheduler continuously adapts task batching and compute resources to minimize power consumption. Festina further performs energy-aware workload consolidation to reduce GPUs' static power consumption via SLO-aware migration. Comparison with four SOTA LLM serving systems and one DVFS-augmented system demonstrates that Festina reduces energy consumption by up to 56% while maintaining parity in SLO attainment (within a 2% margin)
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Wang, Gourav Rattihalli, Aditya Dhakal, Longfei Shangguan, Dejan Milojicic

item.title: PipeSwift: Revisiting Pipeline Parallelism for Large-Scale Completion-Oriented Agentic LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2609.16491v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM agents execute long-horizon workflows where each model response determines the progress of subsequent tool interactions and environment transitions. Unlike chatbot serving, where TTFT and TPOT SLO constraints are critical, agentic workloads are completion-oriented and increasingly governed by job completion time (JCT). This shift challenges existing LLM serving designs optimized around token SLOs. Through a systematic exploration of scheduling and parallelism, we uncover a previously overlooked principle for agent serving: JCT is governed by the balance between prefill and decode efficiency. A prefill-prioritized scheduling policy achieves the best TTFT and the highest decode throughput, yet fails to attain the lowest JCT. This principle further reshapes the parallelism landscape: we show that pipeline parallelism (PP), long overlooked because it offers little decode-latency advantage, can reduce JCT by providing a more favorable balance between prefill and decode efficiency. Based on these insights, we build PipeSwift, an optimized open-source pipeline-parallel runtime integrated with a tailored micro-batch partitioning strategy co-designed with schedule considering the above trade-off, and pipeline-integrated multi-token prediction. Evaluated on real coding and web-search agent trajectories with two 360B+ MoE models on 64 H800 GPUs, PipeSwift reduces overall JCT by up to 1.45$\times$ over SGLang wide-EP, 2.33$\times$ over vLLM PP2, and 1.54$\times$ over today's state-of-the-art open-source PD-disaggregated deployment. PipeSwift is open-sourced at https://github.com/wsjdsg/PipeSwift.
item.dc:creator: Shiju Wang, Fei Ren, Fangcheng Fu, Zhanhong Tan, Kairui Li, Jingwei Cai, Kaisheng Ma

item.title: Purlin: Separating Orchestration from the Datapath of Collectives
item.description: arXiv:2609.36954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Distributed inference depends on GPU collective communication that must keep pace with evolving hardware and specialized workloads. However, existing works often couple the semantics, orchestration (where and when data moves), and datapath (how data moves) of collective communication. This coupling makes it costly to adopt new hardware mechanisms and customize communication for applications. We present Purlin, a scale-up communication framework that separates these concerns. At the top of Purlin, we specify collectives as a naming of an input and output layout and a copy or reduction operation. In the middle, we introduce a shared orchestration protocol, Stage, Notify, And Consume (SNAC), which derives coordination from these specifications. Below SNAC sits a hardware-specific datapath we call Atom, which implements two key data movement primitives for collectives: copy and reduce. This separation lets us customize collectives and adopt new hardware mechanisms while reusing orchestration via SNAC. We evaluate Purlin on A100, H200, and B200 GPUs. Across seven collectives, Purlin achieves latency speedups of up to 5.14x and bandwidth improvements of up to 4.50x over baselines. Integrated into SGLang, Purlin improves offline LLM serving throughput and interactivity by 1.13x on average and up to 1.37x over baselines. For online LLM inference, Purlin improves interactivity by 1.26x on average and up to 2.85x, with the largest gain occurring under overload. For diffusion image generation, Purlin reduces end-to-end latency by up to 1.13x.
item.dc:creator: Osayamen Jonathan Aimuyo, Swapnil Gandhi, Christos Kozyrakis

item.title: Optimal Transport Aggregation for Distributed Mixture-of-Experts
item.description: arXiv:2312.09877v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper considers the setting in which local Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models are fitted independently on distributed datasets and must be combined into a single global MoE model. Weighted averaging the local mixtures, whose experts are not aligned across machines, often yields a large mixture with many experts instead of $K$ and does not provide an estimator of the true model parameters. We propose to reduce this large mixture to a $K$-expert MoE by minimizing an expected transportation divergence, in which the transport plan depends on the covariates. A relaxation of this problem separates the experts from the gating network: the experts are computed by a majorization--minimization algorithm, which decreases the objective monotonically, and the gating network is then fitted to the gates implied by the optimal plan, with an explicit bound on the resulting loss. We show that the aggregated estimator is consistent whenever the local estimators are, without requiring the local models to have the same labeling across machines. The procedure only needs a single one-way communication round. Experiments on simulated and real data show accuracy close to centralized estimation at a fraction of its computation time. Our source code is available at https://github.com/nhat-thien/Distributed-Mixture-Of-Experts.
item.dc:creator: Fa\"icel Chamroukhi, Nhat Thien Pham

item.title: VibeServe: Can AI Agents Build Bespoke LLM Serving Systems?
item.description: arXiv:2605.06068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For years, we have built LLM serving systems like any other critical infrastructure, with a single general-purpose stack hand-tuned over many engineer-years to support every model and workload. In this paper, we take the opposite bet and let coding agents automatically synthesize bespoke serving systems for different usage scenarios. We propose VibeServe, the first agentic loop that generates entire LLM serving stacks end-to-end. VibeServe uses an outer loop to plan and track the search over system designs, and an inner loop to implement candidates, check correctness, and measure performance on the target benchmark. In standard serving settings, VibeServe matches vLLM and SGLang on Llama-3.1-8B, and delivers 2.3x the goodput of a tuned SGLang for a 397B MoE model on four AMD MI300As. In five non-standard scenarios, VibeServe outperforms existing systems by exploiting opportunities that generic systems miss, spanning non-standard model architectures, workload knowledge, and hardware-specific optimizations. Together, these results argue that infrastructure software should favor generation-time specialization over runtime generality. Code is available at https://github.com/uw-syfi/vibesys.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Kamahori, Shihang Li, Simon Peter, Baris Kasikci

item.title: OpenAgenet / OAN Yellow Paper: Technical Architecture for Trust-Governed Resource Identity and Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2606.03163v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This yellow paper describes the technical architecture of OpenAgenet / OAN. OAN is a protocol-neutral trust layer for open Agent interconnection and discoverable AI resource products. It specifies the role architecture, \texttt{did:oan} identity objects, registration workflow, governance-backed Root lifecycle enforcement, Root-verified package model, authorization-aware Discovery, Root-issued infrastructure authorization VCs, signed trusted invocation, verification requirements, state transitions, security properties, implementation boundaries, and deployment considerations. The design is intended to support heterogeneous Agent frameworks and interaction protocols, including MCP, A2A, ANP-like systems, domain-specific Agent protocols, Skills, MCP Servers, and Tool/API resources. OAN does not define the entire business conversation among Agents or the native protocol of every resource; it defines how resource identities become admissible, discoverable, verifiable, and safe to approach before protocol-specific interaction begins.
item.dc:creator: Jinliang Xu

item.title: FractalNet-Based Heterogeneous Federated Learning for Orbital Edge Intelligence in Satellite Mega-Constellations: A Wildfire Case Study
item.description: arXiv:2609.00875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Satellite mega-constellations are emerging as large-scale sensing, communication, and computation fabrics, yet their learning architectures remain largely inherited from terrestrial federated learning and ground-centric mission operations--- ill-suited to satellites that differ by orders of magnitude in Size, Weight, Power, and Cost (SWAP-C), radiation tolerance, link availability, and propagation delay. We propose a heterogeneous federated learning method based on the FractalNet architecture for orbital edge intelligence. We formalize contact-window-constrained, depth-heterogeneous federated optimization and introduce a distributed path scheduler that assigns model depth as a function of SWAP-C constraints, predicted inter-satellite contacts, and training statistics. To reduce message overhead and energy consumption, each tier pools updates periodically rather than at every contact opportunity, and a three-tier agentic control plane governs in-space scheduling, anomaly escalation, and policy-governed autonomy. As a case study, we apply the framework to wildfire detection, where each orbital shell naturally learns a different semantic level of situational awareness: pixel-scale thermal anomalies at low Earth orbit (LEO), regional fire-front dynamics at medium Earth orbit (MEO), and larger-scale risk propagation at geostationary or high Earth orbit (GEO/HEO). Experiments on simulated mega-constellations validate the approach across convergence, communication efficiency, energy adaptation, scheduled-pooling savings, robustness, and latency.
item.dc:creator: Sai Puppala, Bhabani P. Sinha, Koushik Sinha

item.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2609.04748v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Major open-source serving stacks reuse the key-value tensors of a shared prefix by default. We measure what this prefix reuse costs in reproducibility. Holding model, decoding, seed and request order fixed at batch size one, we ran an eighty-episode multi-turn agentic tool-use workload with prefix reuse on and off across two engines and four weight formats. Without prefix reuse, repeated runs reproduced every token and log-probability in all ten configurations. With it, cache-hit and recompute paths diverged on both engines. On llama.cpp with GGUF weights this path divergence rises with quantization: for Qwen2.5-7B over ten independent server histories, it reached 37.4 percent of episodes at 16-bit and 82.5 percent at four-bit. Near-tie decisions became only about 1.2 times as common, while the cache-path change in top-two margins grew 4.9-fold from 16-bit to three-bit. Serving four-bit weights through 16-bit kernels left divergence not detectably different from 16-bit, placing the amplification mainly in the quantized execution path. At Q4_K_M, run-to-run divergence came mainly from llama.cpp's server-level prompt cache: under the canonical episode order it moved divergence by 37.5 points, and at its default, divergence spanned 20.0 to 28.7 percent under five random orders. With cache state restored, each path reproduced exactly while the two still differed. In the tested stacks, cached serving is irreproducible because the cache state is absent from the request and not reset by default. A single-turn bridge shows path divergence reaching task outcomes with no detectable net change in accuracy. We release the harness, logs, and analysis pipeline.
item.dc:creator: Aditi Patodiya

item.title: A BUD You Can Count On: Efficient, Verifiable Membership Proofs
item.description: arXiv:2609.11251v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A block typically changes only a small fraction of blockchain state, yet producing a state root makes validators update an authenticated tree spanning it all. We show how to support verifiable reads from the writes alone. We introduce Block Update Digests (BUDs), that commit to a block's writes and link each key touched in that block to its previous modification. An optional prior-value record lets one successor BUD authenticate the value between modifications, replacing the baseline's two BUD openings. SuperBUDs summarize those writes over longer intervals, letting a reader verify that a value remained unchanged without checking every intervening block. Thanks to BUDs and SuperBUDs, validators can just keep ordinary flat state while still serving proofs of current and historical values, including deletion. We prove soundness and completeness for reads at or after a key's first logged modification when the required proof data is available. In experiments with the baseline format, a 50x increase in state size raises the measured base-BUD cost by just 1.24x. In paired QMDB experiments, lowering its garbage-collection activation threshold raises process CPU time by 1.3-2.7x and device bytes written by 1.6-2.4x relative to its dormant configuration. BUD authentication requires no corresponding relocation of live entries. In the evaluated baseline, two-digest read-layer payloads stay below 800 bytes, and warm hash-path verification takes at most 146 {\mu}s at p99. Authenticated reads need not make validators maintain an authenticated tree over the entire state.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Ranchal-Pedrosa, Cody Littley, Ben Marsh

item.title: Deploying RDMA for Distributed Inference and Training At Scale
item.description: arXiv:2610.12815v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: RDMA can reduce communication overhead in distributed machine learning systems, but realizing these benefits in production requires more than replacing TCP. Variable-size messages, concurrent connections, bursty incasts, and service failures introduce challenges that hardware offload alone cannot address. This paper reports our experience deploying ByteExpress, a software communication layer over hardware RDMA, in ByteDance's parameter-server-based inference and training systems. We present three lessons from the deployment: efficient RDMA requires buffer management across application and transport layers; scalable communication requires coordinated management of connections, receive capacity, and outstanding data; and service availability requires recovery above the transport layer. ByteExpress combines an RDMA-aware allocator, zero-copy transfers, QP multiplexing, receive-credit flow control, a software send window, and RPC-assisted recovery. In production inference, ByteExpress reduces mean and P99 model parameter fetch latency by 35.7% and 43.7%, respectively, and total CPU usage by 10.69% compared with kernel TCP. In training, ByteExpress reduces P99 model parameter push latency by up to 74.0% compared with TCP, with no PFC pauses observed at runtime.
